replication.target_description: Experiment 1: Direct Replication; initial independent-samples lucky-ball versus control comparison of golf putts made (p. 242), before quality-control filtering. Matched by study heading, standard lucky-ball manipulation, golf outcome, and assigned Results locator.

n.sample_role: Participants in two mutually exclusive randomized conditions in the initial primary golf-performance comparison: 58 controls and 66 superstition-activated participants.
n.exclusions: No participants excluded from initial analysis; quality-control-filtered and other exploratory comparisons are separate.
n.location: p. 241 (PDF p. 3), Experiment 1 Participants; p. 242 Results; p. 243 Table 2 note
n.quote: 58 controls and 66 superstition-activated participants ... No participants were excluded from initial ... analysis.

notes: Identity independently checked in canonical text: title Replication of the Superstition and Performance Study by Damisch, Stoberock, and Mussweiler (2010); authors Robert J. Calin-Jageman and Tracy L. Caldwell; DOI 10.1027/1864-9335/a000190; Social Psychology 2014, 45(3):239–245. Primary report with both experiments, methods, results, tables, and references; not abstract-only or preregistration. No PDF supplied; none acquired or rendered. Only assigned unfinished fields populated; other fields are placeholders. Analytic N: 58 controls + 66 superstition-activated participants = 124 participants, no initial exclusions. Separate quality-control subset retains 58 controls and 42 lucky-condition participants and is not the primary initial comparison. Target assignment does not use row order or numeric matching.
